guarantees.claim: When parameter SecMasking is false, sb_in_mask and prd_masking are driven to all-zero bits.
guarantees.cond: always (within the generate block when SecMasking is 0)

assumptions.claim: Modules receiving sb_in_mask and prd_masking when SecMasking is false must ignore these signals safely.
assumptions.risk: If a consumer uses these zero masks as actual masks, data may become unmasked or an attacker may exploit a zero-mask leakage.

uncertain_points.claim: It is not locally enforced that all downstream logic indeed ignores sb_in_mask and prd_masking when SecMasking=0; other modules could misuse these zero values.
uncertain_points.risk: If a downstream module unintentionally relies on these masks for actual masking operations when SecMasking is disabled, it could weaken or bypass masking protections.
